The reference patch antenna had a bandwidth of 143 MHz, a gain of 2.8 dB, and an RCS of -27.98 dBsm.
The PCM structured antenna achieved an RCS reduction of -37.14 dBsm.
The L-structured metamaterial antenna had the lowest return loss of -28.28 dB.
The Square-structured fractal metamaterial antenna had the largest bandwidth of 201.9 MHz.
The gain of the proposed antennas only increased marginally, up to a maximum of 3.2 dB.
The antennas were fabricated using an FR4 substrate with a relative permittivity of 4.4 and a thickness of 1.6 mm.
The target operating frequency of the antennas was 4.3 GHz.
All the antennas used a coaxial feeding technique.
Ansys HFSS software was used for the antenna design and simulation.
The fabricated antennas were measured using a VNA and an anechoic chamber.
The metamaterial loading resulted in a decrease in the radar cross-section for all three fabricated antennas.
A sharp decrease in return loss was achieved by all the antenna designs compared to the reference patch antenna.
A significant increase in bandwidth was reported for all the antennas, with a marginal increase in gain.
The PCM structured antenna achieved the best RCS value of -37.14 dBsm.
The L-structured metamaterial antenna had the lowest return loss of -28.28 dB.
